propositions: Core implements five CAS retry cycles plus exactly one conditional terminal push, with strict delivery as opt-in catchable error and best-effort as default for all existing callers.
Strict push delivery raises reusable PushDeliveryError with pinned stable reasons and is translated to stderr plus nonzero exit only by the Python module adapter, not by core itself.

All pre-existing library, CLI, MCP, importer, and store-write callers omit strict or reach core with strict=False, retaining legacy warning-and-return behavior while inheriting the corrected five-cycle plus one-terminal retry budget.
Strict failure writes no ticket event, emits no BRIDGE_ALERT, and preserves HEAD, worktree, and unpushed commits; dirty-tree staging and committing remain outside push_tickets_branch.
Push-first retry logic with fetch-and-merge recovery only after retriable rejection delivers clean merged HEAD via exactly one terminal sixth push; earlier success returns without terminal push.

All eleven stable rejection reasons (push-disabled, async-delivery-unobservable, invalid-destination, remote-not-found, push-policy-declined, push-transport-failed, merge-recovery-blocked, store-epoch-pre-merge, store-epoch-during-recovery, final-push-rejected, lock-timeout) are machine-stable and distinct between policy decline and transport failure.
